Keralajyo(jyau)tiṣa
MD. 13644 (inc.). 14027 (inc. text different from previous). 18175 [Page043-b] (inc.). MT. 2644 (c) (inc.). R. A. Sastri I. p. 129. II. p.. 171. 206.
--by Acyuta. Adyar II. p. 59a. MD. 13775-9. MT. 853 (a.. 3322. 4056. See NCC. I. Revised edn. p. 72b. Same a. Devakerala.

Keralatattva

Keralapañcapakṣī

Keralapāśāvalī

Keralapurāṇa
Oppert II. 6242. Triv. Cur. V. 39 (108 chs.). Viśvabhāratī 1033.

Keralapraśna(grantha)
jy. on prognostication. Kotah 302. Lucknow Mus. NP. X. 50. Oudh XIV. 52. PUL. II. p. 212.
--ascribed to Garga. Oudh XV. 68.
C.. Mithilā III. 26.

Keralapraśna
See also Praśnakeralī. IM. 1013 (with C.). 1075.

Keralapraśna
prognostication. Mithilā. III 26.
Invokes Kūṣmāṇḍī. Last verse describes the work a. Pāśakakeralī by Garga.
C.. also Keralapāśāvalī by Gargācārya, NP. V. 86 an. Keralapraśna ascribed to Garga, Oudh XV. 68.
--prognostication with areca-nuts. Mithilā III. 180 (Praśnakerala or Keralīyapraśna; see col.).

Keralapraśna
or ke.prakaraNa or keralIyajJAna jy. (Beg. dititanayakSiti) prognostication based on letters. Bomb. Uni. 512. TD. 11685. 24023.

Keralapraśna
67 verses on divination.
Pt.. with Hindi transl., Lakshmipur, Bombay, 1913. See Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1906-28. 489.

Keralapraśna
or divyacUDAmaNi by Keralācārya. Text has agreement with Akṣaracūḍāmaṇi (NCC. I. Revised edn. p. 12) an. Cūḍāmaṇisāra (Alwar. Extr. 475).
Alph. List Beng. Govt. p. 52. Ani. Assam jy. 16 (Pratapcandra Gosvami of Nalbari). Dacca 1452. Gough p. 34. Gov. Or. Libr. Madras 20. 36. Hpr. I. 81 (called Kerali). L. 350. 431. MD. 13937 (Benares Lithograph). MT. 2175 (b) (inc.). (with Telugu C.). Mysore I. p. 342. RASB. X. 7124. Stein 157. [Page044-b]
C.. Cūḍāmaṇikeralī, IO. 3126 etc., a similar text.
Pt.. in Telugu script an. with Telugu gloss. Vavilla Press, Madras, 1914.

Keralapraśnagrantha
by Mūladeva. BORI. 143 of Ā883-84. 388 of 1884-86. 802 of 1884-87. Peters. II. p. 192 (no. 143). III. p. 397 (no. 388). Rgb. 802.

Keralabayālis(ºlīś,_ºliṣo)
Sano Hori Nando 15. Probably same a. one below.
--a name of Uḍudāyapradīpa attributed to Keralācārya.
See NCC. II. p. 289 for same text called Keralīgrantha an. Keralī-racita.
See also below Keralīgrantha.
Pt.. with Oriya metrical transl. in Oriya script. Cuttack, 1910, 1921. See Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1906-28. 1102 an. IO. Pt.. Bk.. 1938, p. 1341.

Keralabṛndāvana
or jJAnapradIpa(ºka, ºpikA) (keralIya) jy. by Padmanābha. Some entries are a..
B. IV. 136. IO. 6376 (a..). L. 1952. MD. 13931-3. 15409. 17369. Mithilā III. 113. MT. 981 (g). 3860 (b) (inc.). Oppert I. 60. 360. 988. II. 550. 3647. PUL. II. p. 218 (2 mss.). TCD. 682D. Ujjain I. p. 55. Ujjain Latest Additions 365.
See Jñānapradīpa also.

Keralabhāgya
(with C.). jy. Adyar II. p. 55a.

Keralabhāṣā_(?)
jy.(?) Cranganore 320.

Keralamantra
Gov. Or. Libr. Madras 20.

Keralamāhātmya
paur. on the mythological origin an. legendary history of Kerala; said to be from Agastyasaṁhitā or Paraśurāmāyaṇa of Agnipurāṇa, Bhūgolakhaṇḍa; in the form of dialogue between Bhṛgu an. Yudhiṣṭhira. Some mss. assign it to Bhūgolapurāṇa. See NCC. I. Revised edn. p.. 26, 32a.
Unspecified mss.
Adyar I. p. 143 (a. (2 mss.). BC. 154. 274. Brahmasva Maṭha 97. CPB. 1043. Cranganore 183. GD. 130. Gov. Or. Libr. Madras 20. Granthappura p. 7, no. 130. Mysore III. p. 4. Oppert II. 6243. Paliyam 78 (inc.). (43 chs.). Taylor I. 162. Tekkemaṭham II. 54A. Tiruvāṅkulam 7. Trav. Uni. 505. 1286A. 1290A (inc.). 1293A (inc.). 13552A. L. 651 (inc.). Trippūṇittura I. 122 (1). Tu7b. 9.
Mss. assigned to Agastyasaṁhitā of Paraśurāmāyaṇa in Agnipurāṇa, Bhūgolakhaṇḍa.
Br. Mus. 115 (107 chs.) (Gargayudhiṣṭhirasaṁvāda). GD. 130. Granthappura p. 7, no. 130. Killimaṅgalattu Mana 85. MD. 2393. 15703. MT. 894. TCD. 151. Trav. Uni. C. 1206.
Pt.. Trichur, 1912.
Mss. assigned to Bhūgolapurāṇa, but same a. the above where ‘Bhūgolakhaṇḍa’ is found instead of Bhūgolapurāṇa. [Page045-b]
IO. 6747. 6748 (inc.). MD. 2392 (chs. 1-55, 56 inc.). Paliyam 17. 77 (a. (chs. 105). PUL. II. p. 151 (107 chs.). Whish 147.
--assigned to Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa an. described a. Garga-Yudhiṣṭhirasaṁvāda; text same a. the above. MD. 2393 (first 5 chs. only mention Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa in Col.).
--assigned to Sahyādrikhaṇḍa of Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa, in 6 Cantos.
Pt.. Trichur, 1912.

Keralamāhātmya
a collection of extracts on the Kerala country an. its religious antiquities (38 chs.). IO. 6942.
Ascribed mainly to Skānda, an. a few ascribed to Brahmāṇḍa, Bhaviṣya, Nārasiṁha an. Brahmāṇḍottara. The Garga-Yudhiṣṭhira-saṁvāda assigned in other mss. to Paraśurāmāyaṇa is assigned here to Skānda.

Keralaratnākara

Keralarahasya

Keralarājayogasāra

Keralavacanāni

Keralavarman
King of Kolattunāḍ in N. Kerala (1423-1446 A. D.); maternal uncle of Rāmavarman (a. of Candrikākalāpīḍa, MT. 2764 an. Bhāratasaṅgraha, MT. 4483); patron of Rāghava (a. of C. Padārthacintana on Yudhiṣṭhira- [Page046-a. vijaya, MT. 5119) an. of his disciple Śaṅkara (a. of Kṛṣṇavijaya).
For details see Contribution of Kerala to Skt. Lit. p.. 58-60.

Keralavarman
(1845-90 A. D.) of Neytallūr palace.
--Ārdrāmahotsava Campū. TCD. 1350.
See NCC. II. p. 167a.

Keralavarman
Valiya Koyil Tampurān, called Kerala Kālidāsa (1845-1914 A. D.); belonged to Lakṣmīpuram Palace, Caṅganāśśeri; married princess Lakṣmībāi of Travancore royal family; student of Ilattūr Rāmasvāmi Śāstrī; patronised by Āyilyam Tirunāl Mahārāja (who also interned him later); an. Viśākham Tirunāl Mahārāja of Travancore. Wrote in Sanskrit an. Malayalam.
--Amṛtamathana. short poem.
--Kaṁsavadhacampū. Composed in 1869 A. D.
Pt.. (1) Tinnevelly, 1888. (2) Trivandrum, 1902. See NCC. III. p. 108b.
--Kṣamāpaṇasahasra in fifty sections.
--Gurupavanapureśastotra in 51 verses.
--Citraślokāvalī.
--(Janma) Nakṣatramālāstuti in 27 verses on Āyilyam Tirunāl Mahārāja.
--Tirunālprabandha. [Page046-b]
--Tulābhāraśataka. Composed in 1870 A. D.
--Daṇḍanāthastotra.
--Nāradīyamahimānuvarṇana.
--Pādāravindaśataka or Śrīmūlaº.
--Yamapraṇāmaśataka. Pt.. 1899.
--Lalitādaṇḍaka. Composed in 1875 A. D.
--Lalitāmbāstotra.
--Vikṭoriyācaritasaṅgraha. Composed in 1887 A. D.
--Viśākhavijaya. kāvya in 20 cantos Pt.. 1900.
--Vyāghrālayeśaśataka.
--Śatrusaṁhāraprārthanāśataka.
--Śākuntalapāramya.
--C. on Śukasandeśa. Pt.. JRAS. 1884.
--Śṛṅgāramañjarī. bhāṇa. Composed in 1868 A. D.
--Śoṇādrīśastotra.
--Skandaśataka.
See Contribution of Kerala to Skt. Lit. p.. 254-6.

Keralavarman
(1879-1918 A. D.). of Pantalam palace.
--Dharmaśāstraṣṭaka.
--Rāsavilāsa. bhāṇa.
--Śrīkṛṣṇastotra.
See Contribution of Kerala to Skt. Lit. p. 263.

Keralavarman
prince of Cochin an. patron of Vedāntācārya (a. of C. Uttejinī on Kāvyaprakāśa).
See NCC. IV. p. 101a.

Keralavarman
King of Travancore (?)
--C. Subodhinī on Nārāyaṇīya. Turuttikkāṭṭu Kartā II. 9.

Keralavarman(maṭikendra)

Keralaviḍambanādi

Keralaśāstra
jy. America 5102 (Yogabhāvādhyāyaphala). Kavīndrācārya 835.

--MT. 1981 (d) (inc.). Col. calls it Keralaśāstra; deals with the twelve bhāvas. Col. zrIviracitAyAM has evidently some gap. [Page047-b]
Pt.. English transl. only. ‘Missing Links’ of Hindu Astrology. no. 11. Bombay, 1963.

Keralahorāvyākhyā
jy. by Sarvartu Paṇḍita, written a. the instance of Gopāla a. Vijayanagar. PUL. II. p. 213.

Keralācāra(nirṇaya)
on peculiar customs of Kerala. Tekkemaṭham I. 65K. Trav. Uni. 1186B (inc.). 2071A. 5054D. 6115C. L. 625B. L. 1269Z-1 (inc.).
--on 64 anācāras or peculiar customs of Kerala, ascribed to Śaṅkarācārya. MT. 3420 (b). Trav. Uni. C. 913B.
C.. Laghudharmaprakāśikā or Śaṅkarasmṛti ascribed to Śaṅkarācārya; also Ācāranirṇaya.

Keralācāradīpikā
paur. on legendary history an. customs of Kerala. MT. 5250 (chs. 7-73). 7275 (chs. 60-64, 65 inc.) (wrongly ascribed to Bilvamaṅgala). Composed a. the request of one of the kings of Cirakkal (Kolāttiri) in N. Malabar.
Pub. by Jnanasagaram Book Depot, Trichur, 1929.

Keralācārasaṅūgraha
MT. 3633 (a. (inc.). Trav. Uni. 1186B. 1205C (inc.). L. 1269Z-2 (inc.).

Keralācārya
--Keralapraśna or Divyacūḍāmaṇi. jy. See above. IM. 10737 notes a Mātrācūḍāmaṇi by a Kevalācārya who may be Keralācārya.

Keralābharaṇa
or Rasasarvasvacampū on the model of Viśvaguṇādarśa; on the customs an. manners of people in different parts of South India with special reference to Kerala; in the form of a dialogue between Vasiṣṭha an. Viśvāmitra. by Rāmacandramakhin, son of Keśava Dīkṣita an. belonging to the family [Page048-a. of Ratnakheṭa Dīkṣita; beg. of 18th Cent. A. D. Salutes God a. Anantaśayana (Trivandrum) an. is acquainted with Kerala.
Burnell 168a. GD. 1621. Gough p. 188. Granthappura p. 80, no. 1621. MT. 5226 (inc.). Mysore 9. TD. 4031-34. Trav. Uni. 1484B. 8627C.
See Contribution of Kerala to Skt. Lit. p. 240.

Keralāhnika

Keralī

Keralī
